name: Acme Pharmacy (example)
description: Example workspace: a Tier-0 pharmacy claims platform failing over from us-east-1 to us-east-2. It runs in three environments — production (the estate the business is promised), staging (in us-east-2 on purpose), and dev (where the recovery tests actually run) — and is made of five services: adjudication, remittance, pharmacy, pricing, and the shared platform layer they all ride on. The data comes across on AWS-native replication (Aurora Global Database, S3 Cross-Region Replication, ECR replication, Secrets Manager replica secrets, AWS Backup copies) and the shape is rebuilt from Terraform and GitOps; two components are still recovered by a third-party tool, so both models sit side by side. Three components are deliberately left unassigned to an environment, because in a real inventory some always are. A program mid-flight, with real gaps. Explore it, then create your own workspace.

environments.name: Production
environments.notes: The estate the business is promised. Every objective in services.json with a BIA source belongs to this environment, and it is the only environment with approved objectives. It is also the environment that has never been recovered: every recovery test so far has run in dev. The resource graph and the Kubernetes snapshot in this workspace are both production (account 111122223333, us-east-1).

environments.name: Staging
environments.notes: Pre-production, and deliberately in us-east-2 — the region production would fail INTO is a region we operate every day, so capacity, quotas, AMIs and instance types there are not a first-time discovery at T0. Staging itself is NOT recovered in an event: if its region went dark it would be rebuilt from Terraform and reloaded from a masked snapshot. It is inventoried thinly (11 components, captured from account tags) because nobody has walked it the way dev was walked; treat the gaps as unknown, not as absence.

environments.name: Dev
environments.notes: Where the Phase-1 recovery tests actually run: the dev estate is recovered into us-east-2 on the same runbook, with the same mechanisms, at a smaller size. That is why it is the most completely inventoried non-production environment here. The numbers the workspace quotes (47-min RTA, 118-min RPA) were measured in THIS environment on 2026-08-28, not in production. Dev carries no business objective of its own — it exists so the procedure is proven somewhere before it is needed somewhere else.

objectives.notes: RTO/RPO are proposed, not yet approved by the business. The 47 and 118 were typed in here by hand after the August dev test — and that test FAILED, so they are a time to failure, not a recovery time. Do not quote them to anyone. They stay on file to show what is still unproven: until a test passes and measures them, this program has no recovery number. The 118 came from the remittance cluster, the one store still on point-in-time recovery, so it is the worst store rather than the system.
